approved: Governor-General Amendment (Cessation of Allowances in the Public Interest) Bill 2023
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would allow the government to end pension-like payments to ex-governors-general or their surviving partners if the former officeholder committed serious wrongdoing.
The minister could issue a legislative instrument to stop the payments, or either house of parliament could pass a resolution to the same effect.
The change would start the day after the bill receives royal assent.
Creates a power to stop allowances to former governors-general or their spouses for serious misconduct.
Allows the minister to make a declaration through a legislative instrument to cease payments.
Allows a house of parliament to pass a resolution to cease payments.
Former governors-general and their spouses who receive allowances under the Governor-General Act 1974.
